newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down 30 bps to 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down 30 bps to 11 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate fell 30 basis points to 11 percent on Thursday, as good supply of kuna funds pushed down the benchmark call money rate at Zagreb money market.
Daily trade totalled a modest 24.2 million kuna, against 100 million kuna on offer.
Fresh borrowings accounted for 19 million kuna, mostly call money granted at a rate of 10 percent, 50 basis points down from the rate that has been steady for months.
Dealers put down the slide to a "strong rise in supply of kuna funds".
The only other fresh borrowing was a two-month loan granted to a saving bank at 18 percent a year.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at 9-14 percent and banks extended old two-week and one-month borrowings at 12 and 15 percent, respectively.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday weaker at 6.1438 against the dollar and 3.5776 against German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
